result.document_summary: California Civil Code section 1950.6, the state statute governing residential rental application screening fees (as amended effective January 1, 2026).
result.notes: One rule extracted: the application screening fee cap and conditions. Rules in the section on receipts, refunds, and credit report copies are treated as part of the same screening-fee regime. Statute applies to all residential rental property landlords with no stated coverage limits. The $30 cap is CPI-adjusted annually since 1998; the document does not state the current adjusted amount.

rules.title: Application screening fee cap and conditions
rules.requirement: A landlord may charge an application screening fee no greater than actual out-of-pocket screening costs (including reasonable value of time), and never more than $30 per applicant (CPI-adjusted annually since 1998). No fee may be charged if no unit is or will soon be available, and the landlord must offer a first-come-first-served process or refund the fee to unselected applicants within set deadlines, give an itemized receipt, and return unused amounts.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.coverage_text: Applies to any landlord (owner of residential rental property) or their agent who charges an applicant a screening fee when renting a residential unit.
rules.interaction: Applies notwithstanding Cal. Civ. Code § 1950.5 (the application fee is not treated as security); does not preempt rules on deposits and fees under federal or state housing assistance programs; does not prevent a landlord from accepting a reusable screening report under § 1950.1.
yields_to: Federal or state housing assistance program provisions governing deposits and fees
